questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Concrete Constituents & Mix Design Principles
questions.text: Explain Bogue's Compounds in Ordinary Portland Cement ($C_3S, C_2S, C_3A, C_4AF$) and their contributions to early strength, ultimate strength, rate of hydration, and heat generation. Explain tests for initial and final setting times using Vicat's apparatus and soundness test using Le Chatelier's apparatus.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Concrete Constituents & Mix Design Principles
questions.text: Explain Abrams' Water-Cement Ratio Law and Gel-Space Ratio theory. What is the Fineness Modulus (FM) of fine aggregates and coarse aggregates? Explain the Bulking of Sand phenomenon and its practical significance on site batching.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Fresh & Hardened Concrete Properties and Durability
questions.text: Define Workability of concrete. Explain factors affecting workability. Describe and compare: (a) Slump Test, (b) Compacting Factor Test, and (c) Vee-Bee Consistometer Test for different ranges of workability. What are Segregation and Bleeding in fresh concrete and how are they controlled?

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Fresh & Hardened Concrete Properties and Durability
questions.text: Explain Compressive Strength, Split Tensile Strength, and Flexural Strength (Modulus of Rupture $f_{cr} = 0.7\sqrt{f_{ck}}$) of hardened concrete. Explain Creep and Shrinkage in concrete structures.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Concrete Constituents & Mix Design Principles
questions.text: Design an M25 concrete mix conforming to IS 10262:2019 guidelines for moderate exposure conditions. Target mean strength $f'_{ck} = f_{ck} + 1.65 s$. Standard deviation $s = 4.0\,\text{N/mm}^2$. Maximum size of aggregate is $20\,\text{mm}$ (angular). Minimum cement content $300\,\text{kg/m}^3$ and maximum water-cement ratio $0.50$. Calculate proportions of water, cement, fine aggregate, and coarse aggregate.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Concrete Constituents & Mix Design Principles
questions.text: Explain Chemical Admixtures (Plasticizers, Superplasticizers, Retarders, Accelerators) and Mineral Admixtures (Fly ash, Silica fume, GGBS). Explain Self-Compacting Concrete (SCC), Fiber-Reinforced Concrete (FRC), and High-Performance Concrete (HPC).

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Concrete Constituents & Mix Design Principles
questions.text: Explain the structural design principles of load-bearing brick masonry according to IS 1905. Define basic compressive stress, permissible compressive stress ($f_c = f_b \times k_s \times k_a \times k_p$), Stress Reduction Factor ($k_s$), Area Reduction Factor ($k_a$), and Shape Modification Factor ($k_p$).

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Fresh & Hardened Concrete Properties and Durability
questions.text: Explain Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) methods for concrete: (a) Rebound Hammer Test, and (b) Ultrasonic Pulse Velocity (UPV) Test. Discuss factors affecting durability of concrete (Alkali-Silica Reaction - ASR, Sulfate attack, Carbonation, and Chloride ingress).

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Design of Masonry Walls for Axial & Eccentric Loads
questions.text: Design a load-bearing brick masonry interior wall of height $3.2\,\text{m}$ carrying an axial compressive load of $180\,\text{kN/m}$. The wall is supported by RCC floor slabs at top and bottom. Compressive strength of bricks is $10\,\text{MPa}$ and cement mortar 1:4 is used.
